official.programme: Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters Scholarship (EMJMD) - Erasmus+
official.university: European Commission - European Education and Culture Executive Agency (EACEA)
official.funding_label: Full scholarship for the best-ranked students
official.deadline_note: The European Commission states that students apply directly to the institution running their chosen programme, and that in most cases applications are submitted between October and January for courses starting the following academic year. Each master's own website sets its own deadline.
official.application_cycle: Annual intake; a new batch of selected Erasmus Mundus Masters is added to the list each year
official.status_note: The Commission's page is live and invites students to search the course catalogue for details of the latest programmes on offer and to apply directly to the institution running their chosen programme. There is no single central deadline.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Scholarships cover your participation costs and contribute to travel, visa, a living allowance. Masters may also offer full scholarships to the best-ranked students worldwide.
benefits: Full scholarships to the best-ranked students worldwide, covering participation costs and contributing to travel, visa and a living allowance

Study at several universities in Europe and beyond: each Erasmus Mundus Joint Master involves at least 3 higher education institutions from at least 3 different countries, plus multiple associated partners

A joint qualification on completion: either a joint degree, one single degree certificate issued on behalf of at least two higher education institutions, or multiple degrees, at least two degree certificates issued by two higher education institutions of the consortium
Typically includes periods of study, research, traineeship, thesis preparation and defence
Students from all over the world are welcome
Erasmus Mundus students and alumni can join the vibrant student and alumni network
eligibility: Have a bachelor's degree (first degree), or be in your last year of bachelor studies
You will need to graduate before the master's programme starts
You may also apply if you demonstrate a bachelor's equivalent level of learning, officially recognised according to national legislation and practices in the degree awarding country
Students who previously obtained an EMJM scholarship are not eligible for an additional EMJM scholarship
requirements: Students apply directly to the institution running their chosen programme
Search the course catalogue for details of the latest programmes on offer
Each master's website has all the details about the course of study, the list of participating universities, the entry requirements and all the steps of the application process
Consult the FAQ of each individual Master before completing your application to make sure you meet the requirements
documents: Bachelor's degree certificate, or proof that you are in your last year of bachelor studies and will graduate before the programme starts
The admission documents required by the consortium, which are listed on each master's own website
selection_criteria: Masters may offer full scholarships to the best-ranked students worldwide
Each master's own website lists the entry requirements and the full application process, and scholarships are applied for within that application
coverage: The OeAD, Austria's National Agency for Erasmus+, publishes the Erasmus Mundus Joint Master as full-time scholarships of 1,400 euros per month for excellent students from Austria, Europe and around the world
application_method: Search the Erasmus Mundus course catalogue published by the EACEA for the latest programmes on offer
Consult the FAQ and the entry requirements on the chosen master's own website
Apply directly to the institution running the programme, within the deadline it sets
Apply for the Erasmus Mundus scholarship through the same consortium application
official.application_route: Choose a programme in the EACEA Erasmus Mundus catalogue and apply directly to the consortium, which also handles the scholarship application.
official.citizenship_residency: Students from all over the world are welcome
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the Commission states that students from all over the world are welcome
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Each joint master is jointly designed and delivered by a consortium of at least 3 higher education institutions from at least 3 different countries, with multiple associated partners from the academic and professional worlds; each master's own website specifies its entry requirements
official.duration: 1 to 2 academic years, typically 60, 90 or 120 ECTS credits
official.description: Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters are prestigious, integrated international study programmes, jointly designed and delivered by an international consortium of higher education institutions. Students apply directly to the institution running their chosen programme, and masters may offer full scholarships to the best-ranked students worldwide.
official.program_type: Joint international master's degree programme with EU-funded scholarship

verification.notes: The programme structure, consortium requirement, joint or multiple degree outcome, typical period structure, eligibility including the previous-EMJM-scholarship exclusion, the direct-to-consortium application route, the October to January timing window, and the scholarship components (participation costs, travel, visa, living allowance) were read on the European Commission's own Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters page and the EACEA course catalogue. The Commission's page lists the scholarship components but does not state a monthly amount; the EUR 1,400 per month figure is published by the OeAD, Austria's National Agency for Erasmus+, on its own programmes page. Travel coverage is inferred from the Commission's statement that scholarships contribute to travel, so it is recorded as true.

applicant_utility.summary: An Erasmus Mundus Joint Master is the only EU scholarship route that bundles study at several universities in Europe and beyond into a single degree, and the scholarship is deliberately broad: participation costs, travel, visa costs and a living allowance. The monthly figure that national agencies circulate - EUR 1,400 per month, per the OeAD - is a useful planning number, but the European Commission's own page lists the components rather than the amount, so always confirm the exact award on the individual master's page before rejecting or accepting an offer. There is no central deadline; you apply straight to the consortium.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Ambitious students who want two or more countries in one master's and who are comfortable that entry requirements, deadlines, the scholarship application itself and even the language requirements are set separately by each of the 200-plus masters. The best candidates are those who already know which consortium they want, have read that master's FAQ, and can state why they need that specific multi-country curriculum.
application_readiness_checklist: Open the EACEA Erasmus Mundus course catalogue and shortlist masters in your field
Check on each master's website whether the field, country combination and curriculum match what you want
Read each master's FAQ and entry requirements carefully before applying
Confirm you hold a bachelor's degree or are in your last bachelor year and will graduate before the master starts
Confirm you have never previously received an EMJM scholarship
Prepare the transcript, degree certificate or proof of final-year study, CV and motivation letter that the consortium requires
Check the English or other language requirement on that master's own website - it is not set centrally
Apply directly to the institution running the programme, applying for the scholarship within the same application
Submit in time for the consortium's own deadline, which falls in most cases between October and January for a start the following academic year
common_rejection_risks: Applying to the Commission office instead of the consortium - applications go directly to the institution running the programme
Using another university's deadline instead of the one on the chosen master's website
Missing the master's own English language requirement
Applying without proof that you will graduate before the programme starts
Having previously received an EMJM scholarship, which makes you ineligible for another
Assuming all Erasmus Mundus scholarships are the same - the award and process differ per master
Leaving applications until January when popular masters have earlier closing dates
Choosing a master without checking the list of participating universities, only to find the country mix is not what you expected
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: A full scholarship covers participation costs, travel, visa and a living allowance, but if you are ranked below the scholarship threshold you can still be admitted as a self-funded student. In that case you carry the full programme fee rate plus everything the scholarship would have covered. Even as a scholarship holder, confirm on the individual master's page whether the award is the maximum EMJM rate or a partial award.
applicant_utility.document_audit: There is no central document list. The only two things the Commission states are that you hold a bachelor's degree (or are in your last year and will graduate) and, where relevant, a recognised bachelor's-equivalent level of learning; everything else comes from the master's own website. Build a separate document pack per consortium.
alerts: There is no central deadline - each master sets its own, and the Commission says applications are in most cases submitted between October and January for courses starting the following academic year
Students who previously obtained an EMJM scholarship are not eligible for an additional EMJM scholarship
Each Erasmus Mundus Joint Master must involve at least 3 higher education institutions from at least 3 different countries
You will receive either a joint degree, one single certificate issued on behalf of at least two institutions, or multiple degree certificates from two institutions of the consortium
The Commission's page lists the scholarship components but does not state the monthly amount; the EUR 1,400 per month figure comes from national agencies such as the OeAD
submission_workflow: Shortlist masters from the EACEA Erasmus Mundus course catalogue
Read each master's entry requirements, admission calendar, language requirements and FAQ
Prepare a general document pack: degree or final-year proof, transcripts, CV, motivation letter, language proof
Apply directly to the institution running the programme, before its own deadline
Indicate on the application that you wish to be considered for the Erasmus Mundus scholarship
Await admission and scholarship decisions, which are issued by the consortium
If admitted, start the visa and enrolment steps well before the programme begins
